claim:
Removed code (old lines 146-165): MaxLogLines = 20000 and g_logLines; old logOpen() returned false at 'if (g_logLines >= MaxLogLines)' and opened the file with fopen per hook call; old logClose() called fclose; old logf wrote only when 'g_f && g_logLines < MaxLogLines' and emitted '== log line cap reached =='. New code: 'inline bool logOpen() { return true; }' (164) and 'inline void logClose() {}' (165); logf (173-180) now formats into a 2048-byte buffer and calls KP_LOG(chLevelUp, '%s', buf) with no count, cap, or flush step in this file. The only remaining bounding is rotateIfLarge(), which runs once per process and only when !KpLog_HasCore() (lines 1217-1220).

Why it matters: The per-process 20000-line cap and the per-call open/close (which flushed each level-up dump when the hook returned) are both gone from this file. If the KpLog core or fallback sink does not enforce an equivalent size or line cap, and does not flush per line, the log can grow without bound during a session and the last dump lines can be lost on a crash.

claim:
Lines 3-4 say: "KpLog also keeps the fallback file open, so remove()ing it leaves later writes on an unlinked inode: reset through the public API instead." Line 9 still does `static inline void luoHostLogReset(const char* path) { std::remove(path); KpLog_SetFallbackFile(path); }`, so it calls the remove() that the comment warns against, before the public call.

Why it matters: If KpLog_SetFallbackFile() returns early or reuses the existing FILE* when the path is unchanged, the unlink at line 9 detaches the file the logger still writes to. Later INFO lines then go to an unlinked inode, the file at `path` stays empty or missing, and tests that grep it either fail spuriously or, if they assert absence of a line, pass without proving anything. Either the comment or the code is wrong, and the test-host reset is the only thing that makes these log-grep tests deterministic.
